labels.notes: Row partial, unmarked (no **`label`** mark in RegCompleteTail.lean or RegCompleteLength.lean). prop_reg_complete / prop_reg_complete' statements unchanged by this target (#check matches HEAD: E0 scope, IsE0C1CompleteCauchy / E0C1CauchyComplete, IsE0CauchyMaximal => GH ∧ MGH ∧ IsCauchyComplete 2 of e0RegMFlat M); partial stays disclosed for the E0 scope (T-btz-scope) and the readings OQ-142 / DEC-31/35. git diff HEAD on RegCompleteLength.lean: the statement of LFSurgeryData.exists_isCompact_of_cauchySeq (hGH, hS, Dat, hsum, hu ⊢ ∃ K compact, eventually lenPt (u n) ∈ K) is byte-identical; only the body (sorry -> term proof), the import and the module docstring changed. The hypotheses of exists_tendsto_of_cauchySeq_of / exists_isCompact_of_cauchySeq_of are genuinely discharged there, not smuggled: hcomp := hS.complete, hcontS := hS.continuous, htend := tendsto_of_cauchySeq_of_isCompact (proved earlier in the file, l.1102, from S closed via isClosed_of_isCauchySurface hGH hS.cauchy and G4 from hS.reg), hcontX := continuous_regVal ∘ continuous_inducedLengthSpace_toSubtype, hlog := ⟨logRad i, if_pos, ofReal_abs_logRad_sub_le_edist⟩, hsum is the lemma's own hypothesis (removed upstream by exists_summable, as before). Finding on l.1571 accurate: BTZ_1.tex l.1091 says « Since M is Cauchy-compact, it admits finitely many BTZ-lines » and l.1093 asserts Σ* metrically complete without argument; for a Cauchy-complete M with possibly infinitely many BTZ lines the compact proof does not apply verbatim. This is a gap in the printed proof, not a false statement, and the REPORT phrases it as such (no statement changes).
